messages:
Maria Chen: FYI perf regression after yesterday's runtime change — small-batch tail latency increased on nvlink nodes.

Jun Park: Can you paste the nsys snippet? which workload and seq distribution?

Maria Chen: Repro on rtx-a100-nv2 with chat workload (mixed seqs 8 -> 512). Ran a 30s nsys capture. Key command I used: 
```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=/tmp/trace1 --sample=cpu --duration=30 --capture-range=cuda
```

Maria Chen: Timeline shows repeated cudaMemcpyPeerAsync peaks that line up with KV-cache miss storms. H2D/D2H bursts ~3-5ms each — way bigger than before.

Sasha Iqbal: Did the kernel-selection tweak that landed yesterday change the matmul kernel family? that could alter launch sizes and KV access frequency.

Maria Chen: Yes, runtime now prefers the q8h matmul path for short sequences; it's lower-latency per-op but has smaller compute per kernel which increased prefetch frequency.

Liam O'Connor: Can you paste a minimal timeline excerpt (kernel names + durations)?

Maria Chen: ```
[ 12345 ] matmul_q8h.launch            0.42ms
[ 12346 ] kvcache_prefetch_async      0.80ms
[ 12347 ] cudaMemcpyPeerAsync H2D     3.1ms
[ 12348 ] matmul_q4.launch            0.30ms
[ 12349 ] cudaMemcpyPeerAsync D2H     2.9ms
```

Jun Park: That H2D/D2H pair on the hot path is suspicious — prefetch hits should avoid round trips. Are we allocating KV pages as pageable host memory?

Maria Chen: Yes, current allocator path uses host malloc (pageable). I switched to a quick micro-repro that uses cudaHostAlloc(pinned) for the KV buffers and the memcpy spikes disappeared.

Sasha Iqbal: So the chain is: kernel-choice -> more frequent small matmuls -> increased kvcache churn -> more host transfers -> pageable copies blow up latency. Makes sense. :thinking_face:

Liam O'Connor: For a short-term mitigation: (1) if sequence-length variance > 0.35 prefer the batch-coalescing matmul kernel that increases compute/window per transfer; (2) add a small pinned buffer pool for KV prefetch paths to eliminate pageable overhead.

Jun Park: Perf counters show PCIe bandwidth is low but there are many tiny transfers — so bandwidth isn't the issue, latency is. NVLink shows similar behavior but GPUDirectPeer still pays an extra setup cost on pageable buffers.

Maria Chen: I'm preparing a PR to change the default KV allocator to use a pinned pool and to expose an env var to bias kernel selection toward larger-launch kernels under high seq-variance. Will attach perf graphs to the PR.

tracebot: [automated] linked artifact: https://artifacts.redwood/trace/1863007890/trace1.qdrep

Sasha Iqbal: After the PR lands let's run a perfetto trace with synthetic mixes (8/32/256/512) and a stress test that forces kvcache miss storms so we can validate under jitter.

Maria Chen: ack — will add an integration test that simulates KV miss storms and asserts no host-copy spikes above 2ms for sustained periods.

Liam O'Connor: Thanks team. If anyone has a quick repro script drop it here and I'll run it on prod-nvlink pool.

Jun Park: Putting repro in gist: https://gist.github.com/jun/kv-prefetch-repro (synthetic batch generator + nsys command).

Maria Chen: thx — will iterate and post before EOD.
